contracts: Maintainer-authorized input repair at 9cd87d3a; no VDD rerun, Bootstrap or new governance receipt. Existing compiler/terminal/history files are historical, not current execution proof.
Use current Quick Dev controlled probes: present -> regression; missing -> causal RED/GREEN/REFACTOR; mixed -> retain both subsets; unverifiable -> repair harness/environment, never manufacture RED.

The primary selector is Python -m pytest for current CER collection. Q2 authors one pytest case per atomic obligation, marking each required assertion with pytest.mark.cer_assertion. Keep parameter instances individually attributable.

For C# behavior, the pytest case must invoke the real named .NET boundary test with a literal subprocess.run argv list, explicit shell=False, dotnet test PhaseA.Platform.Tests/PhaseA.Platform.Tests.csproj, exact --filter FullyQualifiedName=<mapped case> and --logger trx. The frozen C# Fact/Theory source must call a declared real owner (or WebApplicationFactory<Program> plus CreateClient); its test project must reference the owner project. Then parse a fresh per-invocation TRX, verify the expected case identity and all required parameter results, then assert the actual product observation. A build/discovery/timeout/privilege/setup failure raises a harness error, never an AssertionError labeled as product RED. No skip, xfail, constants, source-text checks or stale TRX as substitute.

Failure IDs belong only to failing bound behavioral assertions. Freeze wrapper, C# case, helpers, fixture and case map before formal RED; GREEN/REFACTOR reuse them byte-for-byte. Include all authored test dependencies in execution_snapshot_paths before freezing; do not edit the plan during GREEN.

Only declared production owners may change after expected RED. Program.cs changes are narrow endpoint/composition changes, never whole-file restructuring. Respect applicable existing protected-path authority; do not widen live/runtime access.

No live metadata/workspace, runtime/Caddy, shared Skill, Taskmaster, model/backend authority or historical evidence writes. Use disposable roots and SQLite; retain failed diagnostics under the explicitly owned logs directory.

Current host/OS/fixture capabilities are checked locally. Real restricted Windows processes, Job Object lifetime, NTFS denial, SQLite restart, authenticated routes and publication must not be mocked. Harmless workloads may isolate unrelated model behavior.

Preserve every bound assertion in the terminal proof. Positive result fields must correspond to actual successful checks; count/exit-code/record existence alone is insufficient. Optional regrouping is not a prerequisite.
All bound assertions have current non-skipped CER cases proving their real boundary outcomes; planned test names, markers, counts, records and historical results alone cannot satisfy closure.
agent_contexts.recovery: Preserve diagnostics; fix only the identified harness or product boundary; re-probe this slice and affected dependents. Never roll back correct behavior for RED.

obligations.expected_behavior: The named verification confirms that child processes created by a production heavy-write operation terminate when the parent runner lifecycle ends.
forbidden_result: Any child process remains running after the parent runner lifecycle ends.
obligations.observable_result: No child process from the exercised heavy-write operation remains alive after runner termination and cleanup.
obligations.state_after: All child processes created by the heavy-write operation are terminated.
obligations.state_before: A production heavy-write operation has created one or more child processes.
obligations.subject: Production heavy-write runner child processes
obligations.trigger: When the parent heavy-write runner is timed out, cancelled, or otherwise terminated.

obligations.expected_behavior: The named verification exercises production heavy-write queue cleanup and confirms that lifecycle resources are cleaned up after the operation ends.
forbidden_result: The cleanup path is not exercised.
Runner lifecycle resources remain active after cleanup completes.
obligations.observable_result: RunnerLifecycle_BoundsChildrenAndWrites observes completion of the production cleanup path without active runner lifecycle resources remaining.
obligations.state_after: Production heavy-write runner lifecycle resources have been cleaned up.
obligations.state_before: A production heavy-write operation has reached a terminal lifecycle condition and still has resources requiring cleanup.
obligations.subject: RunnerLifecycle_BoundsChildrenAndWrites cleanup verification
obligations.trigger: When a production heavy-write queue operation reaches a terminal lifecycle condition.

obligations.expected_behavior: The named verification confirms that a Project never has more than one simultaneous heavy writer; an additional heavy-write request must not begin writing while the current writer remains active.
forbidden_result: Two or more heavy writers execute simultaneously for the same Project.
obligations.observable_result: Observed concurrent heavy-writer count for a single Project never exceeds one.
obligations.state_after: The existing writer remains the only active heavy writer for the Project until it releases exclusivity.
obligations.state_before: One heavy writer is active for a Project and another heavy-write request targets the same Project.
obligations.subject: Per-Project production heavy-write concurrency
obligations.trigger: When an additional heavy-write request is submitted while the same Project already has an active heavy writer.

obligations.expected_behavior: The named verification exercises production heavy-write queue cancellation and confirms that the cancelled operation stops.
forbidden_result: The cancellation path is not exercised.
The cancelled heavy-write operation continues executing.
obligations.observable_result: RunnerLifecycle_BoundsChildrenAndWrites records that cancellation stops the production heavy-write queue operation.
obligations.state_after: The cancelled heavy-write operation is no longer executing.
obligations.state_before: A production heavy-write queue operation is queued or running and can be cancelled.
obligations.subject: RunnerLifecycle_BoundsChildrenAndWrites cancellation verification
obligations.trigger: When cancellation is requested for the production heavy-write queue operation.

obligations.expected_behavior: The named verification exercises the production heavy-write queue timeout path and confirms that the operation is stopped when its configured timeout is reached.
forbidden_result: The timeout path is not exercised.
The heavy-write operation continues running after its configured timeout.
obligations.observable_result: RunnerLifecycle_BoundsChildrenAndWrites records a bounded timeout outcome for a production heavy-write queue operation.
obligations.state_after: The timed-out heavy-write operation has stopped with an observable timeout outcome.
obligations.state_before: A production heavy-write queue operation is running with a configured timeout.
obligations.subject: RunnerLifecycle_BoundsChildrenAndWrites timeout verification
obligations.trigger: When the production heavy-write queue operation reaches its configured timeout.

obligations.expected_behavior: Superseding a Project lease must persist a fencing value in SQLite that is greater than the prior fencing value.

The SQLite fencing value decreases.
The fencing progression is maintained only in memory and is not persisted in SQLite.
obligations.observable_result: SQLite records strictly increasing fencing values for successive Project lease acquisitions or supersessions.
obligations.state_after: The superseding Project lease has a higher SQLite fencing value than the lease it replaced.
obligations.state_before: A Project lease and its current SQLite fencing value already exist.
obligations.subject: SQLite Project lease fencing
obligations.trigger: When a Project lease is superseded

obligations.expected_behavior: A Run holding a stale Project lease or fencing value must fail when it attempts to publish.

obligations.state_before: A Run retains an older Project lease or fencing value after another holder has superseded it.
obligations.subject: Stale Run holder
obligations.trigger: When the stale Run reaches the publication boundary

obligations.subject: Project lease persistence verification
obligations.trigger: When `Lease_PersistsAndFencesPublication` restarts the process after acquiring a Project lease
